title: Prove a goal builds to completion: a 3-node graph, staffed in parallel, landed on one goal
description:

THE HARDENING AND PROOF ROW for this parent - it owns the e2e, the live drive, the docs sweep and the adversarial pass for the whole multi-node feature, so no sibling child files its own evidence row (global rail 21).

- task-f79d38b119984ae1ae51eba887a28b7d - the compiler seals N nodes.
- task-1d7b9df2579c491992b55de791c99f4f - a node is READY only when its HARD dependencies are ACCEPTED.

Per owner ruling comment-fbe64776 the growth path is the sealed multi-node INITIAL graph, NOT graph.request_expansion; the parent's DoD 2 phrase "expansion run" reads as "the sealed multi-node INITIAL graph" throughout.

- README still asserts the retired rule ("an initial plan seals one node, so a goal is built one node at a time and growth goes through a successor goal"). That sentence is now false and this row rewrites it.
- REPLAN stays as-is for exhausted reviews: `apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/replan-successor-port.ts` is NOT retired by this work; only the claim that growth REQUIRES a successor goal is.
- The live lane recipe and its pitfalls are in memories control-room-live-lane-recipe and productize-loop-2026-09-03; the UnAI goal is goal-c9d9850b at `D:/projexts/UnAI/.moe-next/store.sqlite`.
definitionOfDone: OFFLINE e2e over a REAL daemon (no fixtures, real MCP wire, scripted seat double): one goal, ONE approval decision, a sealed 3-node graph with a HARD chain. Assert IN ORDER: node count = 3 on the sealed graph; the two independent nodes are BOTH staffed in one pass while the dependent node is BLOCKED on `depends:`; the dependent node is staffed only after its parent is ACCEPTED; all three deliver, verify and land on the SAME goalRef.

The coverage read is the closing gate: `POST /documents/coverage/read` reports every approved criterion VERIFIED and the goal reaches ready-to-close ONLY then. Assert a NEGATIVE arm in the same test - at 2 of 3 nodes accepted the goal is NOT ready to close - so the gate is not vacuously green.

NO SUCCESSOR GOAL was minted for growth: the e2e asserts exactly ONE goal aggregate exists at the end and that no replan/successor path was taken. Assert by counting goal aggregates in the store, not by the absence of a log line.

LIVE DRIVE on the lane (UnAI at D:/projexts/UnAI, goal-c9d9850b or a fresh goal): a multi-node graph proposed by a real planning seat, approved in the BROWSER, and at least two nodes landed on the same goal. comments.content:
STEP 7(b) — ADVERSARIAL PASS over the WHOLE parent feature's diff (all five children; this row owns it, global rail 21). Every answer is MEASURED at HEAD, with the file and line that decides it.

Q1. TWO WRAPPER PASSES RACE ON THE SAME READY NODE — IS THE CLAIM THE ONLY FENCE?
NO. There are FOUR, and three of them are durable. `createAgentSessionFence.admit` (`agent-session-fence.ts:191-227`) checks, IN ORDER:
  1. the durable WORK CLAIM (`activeClaim`) -> `AGENT_STAFFING_CLAIM_HELD`;
  2. the durable LIVE-CHILD staffing record, which fences a claim that EXPIRED while the child still runs -> `AGENT_STAFFING_CHILD_LIVE`;
  3. an OS liveness probe of that record's `childPid`, which fences an unretired record left by a SIGKILLed wrapper.
Plus the wrapper's own pre-checks (`agent-wrapper.ts:353` `step.claim !== null`, `:356` `staffing.has(workItemId)`).
EVERY unknown FAILS CLOSED WITH ITS OWN CODE: a corrupt claim ledger or unreadable staffing record answers `AGENT_STAFFING_RECORD_UNREADABLE` ("a corrupt claim ledger must never read as 'nobody holds it'"), and a probe outage answers a DISTINCT `AGENT_STAFFING_LIVENESS_UNKNOWN` so it is never mistaken for ordinary contention.
THE TOCTOU that remains is closed one layer down, not by `admit`: `admit` READS, then the caller COMMITS. Two wrappers can both pass `admit`. The commit is version-fenced — `agent-wrapper.ts:256-257` dispatches `work.claim` at `step.claimAggregateVersion`, and the fence's own `append` commits at `expectedVersion: store.getAggregateVersion(aggregateId)` — so the loser takes EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT and spawns nothing. NET: two seats cannot both run one node; the losing pass reports a coded refusal rather than silently double-staffing.

Q2. A DEPENDENCY WHOSE REVIEW IS UNREADABLE RATHER THAN ACCEPTED OR REJECTED — BLOCK OR LEAK?
IT BLOCKS. `isAccepted` (`affordance-read.ts:387-394`) is `readReviewLedger(...).accepted !== undefined`, and an unreadable ledger sets `unreadable: true` while LEAVING `accepted` undefined (`review-read-model.ts:231/237/255` — a malformed round is never partly trusted). So the consumer's `unmet` list keeps naming it and the node stays BLOCKED. The unreadable node's OWN step also blocks: `awaitingVerify = review.unreadable || latestRound?.routing.route === "ACCEPT"` (`affordance-read.ts:409`). NO LEAK in either direction.
THE GAP, and it is real: the consumer is told `depends:<nodeKey>` — the SAME token as "not finished yet". An unreadable producer is therefore indistinguishable from an unfinished one, and the goal waits forever on a message that says nothing is wrong. Fail-closed but NOT DIAGNOSABLE. Follow-up A below; not patched here (task rail 1).

Q3. A dependsOn CYCLE — DOES IT SEAL AND DEADLOCK?
NO. IT REFUSES AT COMPILE, and the answer is a SURVIVING COMMITTED ARM, not a transcript: `apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.test.ts:134` "refuses a dependsOn CYCLE, which only a multi-node graph can express" asserts `COMPILED_PLAN_ADMISSION_REFUSED @ COMPILED_PLAN_PRODUCER` for a<->b plus c->b, AND `store.getAggregateVersion(RUN_ID)).toBe(0)` — nothing sealed. Its own comment names exactly the hazard this question asks about: "a cycle that SEALED would deadlock the dependency gate rather than refuse at the surface: no node is ever READY." A cycle clears every `shapeRefusal` arm (no unknown target, no self-edge, nothing depends on the completion node) and is caught deeper by the graph codec. NO FOLLOW-UP ROW NEEDED — the gate cannot deadlock because the cycle never reaches it.

Q4. WHAT DOES AN OPERATOR SEE WITH THE SEAT LIMIT AT 1?
Two DIFFERENT facts, and the surface keeps them apart — now pinned by a COMMITTED arm in this row's e2e ("staffs one independent node and leaves the other READY, offered and unclaimed"):
  - the unstaffed INDEPENDENT node stays `READY` and still carries its `review.submit` offer: work waiting on a SEAT;
  - the DEPENDENT node is `BLOCKED` with `depends:<nodeKey>`: work waiting on the GRAPH.
In words, `seatLimitWords` (`activity-words.ts:125-133`) says: "This daemon is set to run 1 agent at once. Every seat is busy, so the next ready node waits for one to finish." Correct and unambiguous. That arm is ALSO the positive control for the two-seat parallel arm: same graph, only the limit moves.

Q5. DOES ANYTHING DOWNSTREAM STILL ASSUME ONE NODE PER SEALED GRAPH?
YES — THREE places. All three FAIL CLOSED with a named code or an empty answer; none mis-activates a multi-node graph, and none is on the lane this row proved (the e2e sealed, activated, staffed, verified, landed and closed a 3-node graph end to end, so every one of these is off that path):
  a. `affordance-planning-authorities.ts:151-152` — `const [node, ...extra] = input.nodes; if (node === undefined || extra.length > 0) return EMPTY;`. On ANY multi-node project the browser's `plan.propose` authority MATERIAL goes empty FOR EVERY RUN, including unrelated ones. Fails closed (the browser refuses locally for want of material) but silently, with no code. The compiled lane does not use it. Follow-up B.
  b. `activation-budget-derivation.ts:125` — `if (bearingKeys.length > 1) return refuse("ACTIVATION_BUDGET_NODE_AMBIGUOUS")`, reached only from `effect.activate` (`activation-ingress.ts:248` `runEffectActivateCommand`, registered at `daemon-command-registry.ts:385`) — a DIFFERENT command from the plan approval, which is why the 3-node e2e activates fine. Named code, fail closed.
  c. `foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:170` — `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_MULTI_NODE_UNSUPPORTED` on the foundation-attempt dispatch. Named code, fail closed.
  ALSO STALE-BUT-HARMLESS: `journey-authority-bodies.ts:158-161` still THROWS `a journey graph needs exactly one node id` — the DEMO SEED's payload producer, so `pnpm seed` can still only seal one node; and `compiled-authority-contracts.ts:10-14` documents `dependsOn` as compiling to "NON-BLOCKING PREFERRED_ORDER edges", which is FALSE at HEAD — `compiled-policy-authority-body.ts:145/156` emits `kind: "HARD"` with `edgeKind: "ARTIFACT_CONSUMPTION"`. A stale doc comment on the exact contract this feature turns on. Follow-up C.
